metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process... can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Video data from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, used as inputs for the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate the simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are extracted as (x,y) points from raw traffic video frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no tools or parameters specified for extraction.

nodes_process.node_name: Generate position matrices from vehicle locations
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m₁ E RXxY;
nodes_process.description: Vehicle location points are used to create a position matrix m_t of size XxY. The matrix additionally contains signal state information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, matrix structure described, no tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Stack and down-sample position matrices for state
nodes_process.source_quote: stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s₁: S₁ = {m₁-(N-1),..., m₁}. For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions...
nodes_process.description: Consecutive position matrices from N time steps are stacked to form the state s_t. Down-sampling is applied to reduce input dimensions, resulting in a state matrix of size (N, X, Y).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, 3/4 parameters stated (downsampling factor missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: We adopt a deep neural network termed Q-network to approximate Q* (s, a). The neural network contains several convolutional layers and fully connected layers. The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7...
nodes_process.description: A deep neural network (Q-network) is defined to approximate the action-value function Q*(s,a). It consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and two fully connected (FC) layers, one for Q-value and one for speed/queue prediction in multitask learning.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 concrete tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, mu > 0, omega < 0
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t is defined as a weighted sum of the average speed in the merging area (v_t) and the average queue length at the on-ramp (q_t) during time steps t and t+1.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames... The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w; to minimize the loss function. The experience replay [30] stores the data prepared for training into the replay buffer...
nodes_process.description: The deep Q-network is trained using a deep reinforcement learning approach. This involves an Adam optimizer, experience replay, a target network for stability, multitask learning, and an e-greedy strategy for action selection. The training minimizes a total loss function combining Q-value prediction and speed/queue prediction.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/7 concrete tools named, 8/9 parameters stated (random seed missing).

nodes_process.node_name: Set up microscopic traffic simulation environment
nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, as shown in Figure 5.
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO to model a freeway network connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, including an on-ramp and mainline merge. Simulation time is 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, 4/5 parameters stated (driving behavior parameters missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: The second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is configured as a baseline, which calculates the ramp metering rate based on previous red phase length and downstream occupancies. The green phase length is fixed, and the red phase length is determined by the metering rate.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios
nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds. Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: 20 simulation experiments are conducted for each of three scenarios: DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control. Each experiment is initialized with a different random seed. Key metrics such as travel times, queue lengths, and traffic flows are measured and compared.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, 1/2 parameters stated (random seed missing).

nodes_process.node_name: Conduct perturbation analysis on video data
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas. The sensors applied in PI-ALINEA are located in subarea 2.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is performed to assess the impact of video data information by removing data from different subareas of the control region (divided into 8 subareas). The DRL method's performance (travel time) is evaluated with this perturbed input.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.
